what_passes.locale_fix_confirmed_in_the_field: start_readers.sh now passes its secret guard under LC_ALL=C, where it previously aborted on an unbound "secret\xef". That is the fix from commit eab69a55 working on the real host.

why_blocked.attempt: Ran scripts/start_readers.sh karakeep on the production host. The secret guard passed because install.sh had already generated karakeep.env, so the profile proceeded to pull its images.
why_blocked.outcome: The pull failed part-way with 'no space left on device' while extracting a layer into containerd. Free space had dropped to roughly 966 MB.
why_blocked.operator_error_acknowledged: This run should have been a dry run or a pull-free config check. Starting the profile for real on a host at 95 percent was a misjudgement.

containment.other_hosted_services: 27 containers still up; no unrelated service was affected

requirement_to_unblock.what: The optional reader stacks are heavy: Karakeep pulls Meilisearch and a headless Chrome, Linkwarden pulls Postgres. Together they need several GB.
requirement_to_unblock.host_reality: The 38 GB root is at 95 percent, holding roughly 8.9 GB of images and 14 GB of containerd layers for about eight unrelated projects.
requirement_to_unblock.decision_is_the_owners: Either free host capacity or expand the disk, or accept SA-304 as permanently optional on this node. Pruning other projects' images or volumes is not a call the build agent should make.

what_this_does_not_prove: Any live Karakeep or Linkwarden projection.
An ArchiveWeb.page WACZ import against production, which needs an Owner-captured WACZ and an explicit L2 opt-in.
non_actions: No unrelated project's image, volume, container or data was pruned or modified.
No secret value was printed to terminal, transcript, evidence or Git.
No user content was sent to any reader service.

per_reader_breakdown.note: An earlier version of this record put all four readers behind host disk. That was imprecise: only the two container-backed readers are disk-blocked.

archiveweb_page.mechanism: WACZ file import through scripts/import_wacz.py; no container involved
archiveweb_page.coverage: 3 focused tests pass: blocked before reading input when L2 is off, rejects an unknown content id before copying the file, and imports as an explicit L2 file projection
archiveweb_page.why_not_run_on_production: L2 is off by default (SOCIAL_ARCHIVE_L2_ENABLED defaults to False, and CANONICAL_STATE sets l2_default false), and a real WACZ can only come from the Owner capturing one with ArchiveWeb.page. The import path does not parse WACZ structure, it stores the file by content address, so running it with a synthetic file would prove nothing the focused tests do not already prove while injecting a bogus L2 artifact into production.

karakeep.mechanism: Docker: app plus Meilisearch plus headless Chrome

disk_headroom_update_20260803T0727Z.why_it_improved: Transient build pressure cleared and containerd released the layers orphaned by the failed reader pull and the image rebuild.
disk_headroom_update_20260803T0727Z.assessment: Karakeep alone might now fit, since it needs roughly 2-3 GB. It is still tight: no margin on a host at 90 percent that serves eight production services, and one disk-full incident has already happened on this node today.
disk_headroom_update_20260803T0727Z.recommendation: Do not retry unattended. If the Owner wants SA-304 closed, retry Karakeep alone with the disk watched, or free host capacity first. Retrying on my own initiative after having already caused one disk-full incident would not be justified.
